# opentel-mcp

> opentel-mcp is a Node.js OpenTelemetry instrumentation library for Model
> Context Protocol (MCP) servers. It detects silent failures —
> CallToolResult.isError: true inside an otherwise-successful JSON-RPC 2.0
> response — and marks the OpenTelemetry span ERROR, something standard
> OpenTelemetry instrumentation misses by default.

Author: Thirumalaiboobathi B. License: MIT. Current version: 0.4.0.
npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/opentel-mcp
GitHub: https://github.com/Thirumalaiboobathi/opentel-mcp

This file follows the llms.txt convention (https://llmstxt.org). For the
full text of every page below concatenated as markdown, see
https://opentel-mcp.dev/llms-full.txt.

## Docs: Introduction

- [Docs overview](https://opentel-mcp.dev/docs): Index of all opentel-mcp documentation, grouped by Introduction, Concepts, Reference, and Guides.
- [Getting Started](https://opentel-mcp.dev/docs/getting-started): Install opentel-mcp and wrap an MCP server's tools/call handler with instrumentMcpServer() — the real 30-second quickstart from the package's own README, including captured terminal output.

## Docs: Concepts

- [Silent Failures](https://opentel-mcp.dev/docs/silent-failures): What a "silent failure" is in MCP (a JSON-RPC 2.0 response that succeeds while CallToolResult.isError is true), the exact MCP specification text on tool execution errors, and how opentel-mcp's isToolResultError() check detects it.
- [Deep Failure Fingerprinting](https://opentel-mcp.dev/docs/deep-fingerprinting): How opentel-mcp v0.4.0 computes a stable 16-hex-character SHA-256 fingerprint per failure, the 8 failure categories, and why only category and origin (not the fingerprint itself) are safe on a metric label.

## Docs: Reference

- [Metrics](https://opentel-mcp.dev/docs/metrics): The four mcp.tool.* OpenTelemetry metrics instruments (calls, errors, silent_failures, duration), with SigNoz and Prometheus/PromQL query examples.
- [API Reference](https://opentel-mcp.dev/docs/api-reference): Real exported signatures — instrumentMcpServer(), InstrumentOptions, computeFingerprint(), toSpanAttributes(), and the fingerprinting types — copied from the package's own TypeScript declarations.

## Docs: Guides

- [Migration Guide](https://opentel-mcp.dev/docs/migration): Migrating an MCP server from hand-written @opentelemetry/api span code to instrumentMcpServer(), with before/after code and a post-migration checklist.

## Answers to common questions

- [FAQ](https://opentel-mcp.dev/faq): 20 developer-intent questions — what a silent failure is, whether opentel-mcp works with SigNoz/Jaeger/Honeycomb/Grafana Tempo, whether it can crash your server, Node.js version support, and an explicit correction of the common assumption that it works with fastmcp (it doesn't — fastmcp is Python; the real connection is a filed-and-fixed upstream bug report).

## Comparison and version history

- [Comparison](https://opentel-mcp.dev/comparison): How opentel-mcp compares to raw @opentelemetry/api instrumentation, with an honest explanation of why fastmcp and "mcp-tracer" aren't included as feature-comparison columns.
- [Changelog](https://opentel-mcp.dev/changelog): Version history v0.1.0 through v0.4.0, sourced from the real commit history and CHANGELOG.md, including a known type-declaration gap in v0.4.0.

## About and blog

- [About](https://opentel-mcp.dev/about): Author bio — Thirumalaiboobathi B, GenAI & Full Stack Engineer in Madurai, Tamil Nadu, India; AWS User Group Madurai Builder Circle Owner; Madurai AI Community member.
- [Blog: Introducing Deep Failure Fingerprinting in opentel-mcp v0.4.0](https://opentel-mcp.dev/blog/introducing-deep-failure-fingerprinting): The problem Deep Failure Fingerprinting solves, how the SHA-256-based fingerprint is computed, cardinality safety via the frozen METRIC_SAFE_ATTRIBUTES array, and the testing strategy behind it.
